content.title: Authenticate as standard_user without inheriting administrative-only capabilities
content.intent: Prove that a standard user can authenticate into the normal full-access banking experience without receiving administrative-only view, data, or capabilities.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning over the role/persona input and auth/permission reasoning because the source separates standard_user from admin_user outcomes. Used covering_array at risk-gated strength 3 because auth applies; it degraded to effective strength 1 because there is only one relevant input (persona), so the authoritative combo set enumerated persona=standard_user. Outcome differs from admin_user, so this remains a separate scenario rather than a parameter on a shared path.

content.title: Authenticate as admin_user into the administrative banking view
content.intent: Prove that admin_user authentication lands in the intended administrative experience and exposes admin-distinct information or controls plus authorized administrative capabilities or data.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning over the role/persona input and state/flow reasoning because the source promises a successful authentication transition into an administrative experience for admin_user. Used covering_array at risk-gated strength 3 because auth applies; it degraded to effective strength 1 because there is only one relevant input (persona), so the authoritative combo set enumerated persona=admin_user. The admin outcome is materially different from standard_user and therefore warrants its own scenario.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied auth and equivalence-partitioning techniques because the documented behavior changes by authenticated persona. Did not apply bva, pagination, CRUD, idempotency, or concurrency because this use-case's grounded evidence did not define ranged inputs, collection semantics, persisted mutation, retry semantics, or competing writes.
